analysis.reproduces_949: No as sustained throughput. Random-weight untied 512x2 (section 43's model) measures 812.4 tok/s wall over a 240 s steady run and 799.5-828.7 in three interleaved 45 s runs; published is 949.

failures.steady-256x8: vkQueueSubmit returned VkResult -4 (VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST) about 80 s into timed steps of roughly 3 s each. Windows Application log: WER LiveKernelEvent code 141 (display engine timeout, TDR) at 22:39:54 and 22:40:21 local. Not retried: a retry would risk another display-driver reset. 256x8 is not re-measured.

load_notes: Before any run: total CPU 1.3-4.6% (Get-Counter, 5 samples) and no python or ollama process above 0.66 CPU-s per 10 s.

During runs, other processes used 0.40-1.15 logical cores of 16 on average (total busy CPU from GetSystemTimes minus the benchmark process's own CPU time). The two runs above 0.9 cores were interleave-r1-C and interleave-r1-D; neither is an outlier in tok/s against its arm's other rounds.

gpu_engine_util_pct_other_sum is other processes' GPU engine utilisation, summed over every process sampled at 1% or more, from one probe per run (two 5 s typeperf samples). It was 43.7-63.2% in all 23 non-preflight runs; at the per-process level that was a desktop app and the desktop compositor, plus at most 1.7% from a browser. The preflight probes (5.5-17.3%, one never fired) ran as or after those 10 s runs ended, with the benchmark process itself at or below 0%. Whether the load during runs is display work competing for the iGPU or an accounting effect of the shared engine was not separated.
analysis.worktree: 40ad1b8 checked out with git worktree add in a scratch directory for arm E, removed with git worktree remove after the runs.
